pages.title: How do I sign in to Tracopus?
pages.description: Open your organization URL, enter username and password on the Luxury login screen, then click Sign In. SSO users click Sign in with Microsoft instead.

pages.title: What is Microsoft SSO?
pages.description: Single Sign-On redirects you to Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). After corporate authentication you return to Tracopus already logged in — no separate password required.

pages.title: I forgot my password — what should I do?
pages.description: Click Forgot Password on the login page, submit your username or email, and follow the reset link. Contact your admin if mail does not arrive within 15 minutes.

pages.title: Why am I stuck on the login page after SSO?
pages.description: Your account may be inactive, not provisioned, or missing a default team. Ask your workspace administrator to verify employee status and role assignment.

pages.title: How do I activate a new employee account?
pages.description: Open the activation link from your welcome email (/user/activateaccount/…), set a password, then sign in. Links expire — request a new invite from HR if needed.

pages.title: Can I stay signed in on my laptop?
pages.description: Yes — sessions persist in the browser. Always sign out on shared machines via the header account menu.

pages.title: Why does my session expire?
pages.description: Security policy may enforce idle timeout or daily re-auth. SSO tenants often require re-login after token expiry — sign in again normally.

pages.title: What landing page do I see after login?
pages.description: Your default module dashboard (Project, HRMS, or Sales) depends on role permissions configured by your administrator.

pages.title: How do I change my password?
pages.description: Account menu → Profile → Security, or use the forced change link at /user/changepassword/… when prompted.

pages.title: SSO user — why is password change hidden?
pages.description: Credentials are managed by your identity provider. Use Microsoft account settings or IT helpdesk for password resets.

pages.title: Where is the main module menu?
pages.description: The left sidebar lists HRMS, Sales, and Project modules. Expand each to see permitted screens for your role.

pages.title: What is the icon rail?
pages.description: The narrow vertical rail on the left edge provides quick links: Search, Taskboard, Calendar, Notes, Chat, Files, theme palette, and settings.

pages.title: How do I change the color theme?
pages.description: Click the palette droplet on the icon rail and pick a Luxury palette (Emerald, Indigo, Sapphire, etc.). Choice syncs to mobile after login.

pages.title: What does SHOW / SORT / Filter mean?
pages.description: Standard list header controls: SHOW = status presets, SORT = column order, Filter = text search on the register below.

pages.title: What is the summary strip?
pages.description: Collapsible KPI and chart row at the top of many list screens. Expand for analytics; collapse for a wider data table.

pages.title: How does global search work?
pages.description: Header search (or icon rail Search) finds projects, tasks, employees, and more. Results respect your team scope and permissions.

pages.title: Why is a sidebar item missing?
pages.description: Your role lacks module or page permission. Administrators enable routes in Application Configuration and role templates.

pages.title: Can I bookmark a screen?
pages.description: Yes — copy the browser URL. Module routes like /hrms/timesheet open directly when you have access.

pages.title: What is the breadcrumb trail?
pages.description: The path under the header (e.g. Home → HRMS → Invoices) shows where you are in the documentation or app hierarchy.

pages.title: How do I collapse the summary charts?
pages.description: Click the summary strip toggle/chevron on list screens — state may persist in browser storage for your session.

pages.title: Where is my personal dashboard?
pages.description: HRMS → Dashboard shows attendance strip, utilization donut, task queue mix, and quick links for the current week.

pages.title: How do I view another employee's profile?
pages.description: HRMS → Employees → click a row. Managers see direct reports; HR admins see the full roster.

pages.title: What is on the employee profile?
pages.description: Tabs for personal info, skills, security, notifications, and activity. Self-service users edit contact details; HR edits org fields.

pages.title: How are departments and bands assigned?
pages.description: Values come from Application Configuration org data (department, band, grade) on the employee wizard and profile.

pages.title: What is utilization on the HRMS dashboard?
pages.description: Billable hours vs capacity for the selected period — read the donut and KPI tiles in the summary strip for trends.

pages.title: Can I export the employee list?
pages.description: Use list export controls if your role includes export permission — typically HR and admin roles.

pages.title: What is attendance vs timesheet?
pages.description: Attendance tracks check-in/out and device events. Timesheet tracks billable/non-billable hours against projects.

pages.title: How do I enable MFA?
pages.description: Profile → Security — follow prompts to register an authenticator if your org requires multi-factor authentication.

pages.title: Who updates my skills list?
pages.description: You or your manager on the profile Skills section. Options are defined in App Config skills key.

pages.title: Why can't I see HRMS at all?
pages.description: Your role lacks hrmsModules visibility flags. Request HRMS access from your workspace administrator.

pages.title: What is the employee create wizard?
pages.description: Multi-step flow: personal details, org assignment, skills, and security — used by HR when onboarding new staff.

pages.title: How do team filters work on HRMS lists?
pages.description: Header team scope limits rows to your org unit or selected team — managers often default to their delivery team.

pages.title: Where do I log hours?
pages.description: HRMS → Time Sheet — weekly grid with billable project rows, non-project categories, and leave types.

pages.title: How do I pick the correct week?
pages.description: Use the week selector in the header. Past weeks may be read-only depending on role policy (enablePastTimeSheetView).

pages.title: What is a work item on the timesheet?
pages.description: A granular activity under a deliverable/project. You log hours against work items when billable project time is required.

pages.title: Can I copy last week's rows?
pages.description: Use copy/pre-fill actions if enabled on your timesheet — saves re-selecting the same projects each week.

pages.title: Why is last week locked?
pages.description: Role policy may set disableLastMonthAfterXDays — after day X of the month, prior month becomes read-only for payroll.

pages.title: What are non-project hours?
pages.description: Internal categories (training, admin, PTO) configured in App Config — separate from client billable project rows.

pages.title: How do managers approve timesheets?
pages.description: Approval workflows depend on org setup — check HRMS settings and your role's approve flags; some orgs use export-only review.

pages.title: Why can't I add a project row?
pages.description: Project may be closed, you may not be a member, or enableTimeSheetEdit is false for your role.

pages.title: What is max hours validation?
pages.description: Daily caps from role config (maxHoursAllowedToEnter) prevent accidental over-entry — split across rows if needed.

pages.title: Mobile timesheet — same rules?
pages.description: Yes — mobile HRMS timesheet respects the same permissions and week locks as the web app.

pages.title: How do billable hours reach an invoice?
pages.description: Approved billable timesheet hours aggregate into the invoice pool for the billing period on HRMS → Invoice.

pages.title: What happens if I forget to submit?
pages.description: Hours may remain draft — managers and finance reports show gaps. Catch up before month lock date.

pages.title: How do I create a project?
pages.description: Project → Project List → Create (if permitted). Link account, team, dates, and optional purchase order.

pages.title: What is a deliverable?
pages.description: A planned outcome or task within a project — has status, estimates, assignees, and child work items.

pages.title: What is a work item?
pages.description: Granular unit of work under a deliverable where time is logged and progress tracked.

pages.title: How do I open the taskboard?
pages.description: Project → Task Board or icon rail shortcut — Kanban columns: Planned, To do, In progress, Done.

pages.title: What is team capacity?
pages.description: Project → Team Capacity shows allocation and availability charts for staffing decisions.

pages.title: How do project members get access?
pages.description: Project Details → Members tab — add employees with appropriate project role. They then see the project in lists and timesheet.

pages.title: What is a project account?
pages.description: The client or org node from Accounts — ties billing, invoices, and reporting to the customer record.

pages.title: Can a project link to a purchase order?
pages.description: Yes — when Sales PO exists, link on project create or details for AP alignment and revenue tracking.

pages.title: Where are project files?
pages.description: Project → File Manager or project details Files panel — folder tree with upload/download per permissions.

pages.title: What is project feedback?
pages.description: Project → Feedback captures client or internal feedback records linked to delivery milestones.

pages.title: How do I run project reports?
pages.description: Project → Reports — catalog of utilization, status, and financial reports filtered by team and date.

pages.title: What closes a project?
pages.description: Status transition to Complete/Closed on project details — may lock new timesheet rows depending on policy.

pages.title: What is the project dashboard?
pages.description: Summary KPIs, health charts, and active deliverables for projects you manage or belong to.

pages.title: How does global project search work?
pages.description: Project → Search or header search — finds projects, deliverables, and tasks by keyword within scope.

pages.title: Where are bid requests?
pages.description: Sales → Bid Requests — pipeline list from intake through won/lost with status chips and filters.

pages.title: How do I create a bid?
pages.description: Click Create on Bid Requests — fill commercial details, account, and study type from configured dropdowns.

pages.title: What happens when a bid is won?
pages.description: Workflow may spawn a purchase order and optionally a project — follow your org's sales-to-delivery handoff.

pages.title: Where are purchase orders?
pages.description: Sales → Purchase Orders — contract records linked to accounts and often to projects.

pages.title: Why do invoices need a PO number?
pages.description: Client AP teams reject invoices without PO reference — copy PO from Sales when creating HRMS invoices.

pages.title: Can I attach files to a bid?
pages.description: Bid Details includes documents panel — upload RFP, proposals, and signed contracts per permissions.

pages.title: What statuses does a bid pass through?
pages.description: Typical flow: Draft → Submitted → Under review → Won / Lost — exact labels from App Config sales lists.

pages.title: Who can see all bids?
pages.description: Sales managers and admins with cross-team scope — ICs often see only assigned accounts.

pages.title: How do bids link to projects?
pages.description: On win, link PO and create project with bid reference — traceability from sales pipeline to delivery.

pages.title: What is bid details vs list?
pages.description: List is the register; Details is single-record view with tabs, timeline, files, and status actions.

pages.title: Where is the invoice list?
pages.description: HRMS → Invoice — billing register with status, amount, account, and fiscal year scope.

pages.title: How are invoice amounts calculated?
pages.description: Primarily from approved billable timesheet hours × rates, plus manual adjustments on invoice details.

pages.title: What invoice statuses exist?
pages.description: Draft → Pending → Approved → Paid → Closed (labels may vary by org configuration).

pages.title: How do I create an invoice?
pages.description: Click Create on the invoice list — pick account, billing period, and billable pool (permission required).

pages.title: Where is the PDF?
pages.description: Open invoice → Invoice Details → PDF preview or download after lines are finalized.

pages.title: What is the fiscal year selector?
pages.description: Filters register and summary charts to the selected FY — important for monthly billing bar trends.

pages.title: Can I invoice without a project?
pages.description: Some orgs allow manual line items — default is project-linked billable hours from timesheet.

pages.title: Who marks an invoice paid?
pages.description: Finance role typically — updates status and summary KPI tiles on the list.

pages.title: Why is my draft missing hours?
pages.description: Timesheets for the period may be unapproved or still open — lock and approve before billing.

pages.title: What is the outstanding panel?
pages.description: Summary chart showing open amounts awaiting payment within the active FY filters.

pages.title: How do I register my phone?
pages.description: After web login, open mobile User Login and scan the QR code from HRMS Settings → device registration.

pages.title: Can I use PIN or biometric login?
pages.description: Yes — after QR registration, set PIN or enable Face ID / fingerprint on the mobile login screen.

pages.title: Does mobile show the same projects?
pages.description: Mobile Projects lists assigned projects — tap for summary; deep links may open web for full details.

pages.title: Mobile timesheet vs web?
pages.description: Same data and permission rules — log hours on mobile when away from desk; week locks apply equally.

pages.title: What are mobile insights?
pages.description: Personal analytics charts: utilization, status mix, and weekly trends — mirrors web HRMS dashboard concepts.

pages.title: Why did QR registration fail?
pages.description: Ensure web session is active, camera permission granted, and device registration enabled in org settings.

pages.title: Can admins use App Config on mobile?
pages.description: No — Application Configuration is desktop admin only. Use a full browser session.

pages.title: Do theme palettes sync to mobile?
pages.description: Yes — palette choice on web syncs after mobile login refresh.

pages.title: How do I log out of mobile?
pages.description: Use sign out on mobile profile/settings — also revoke device in HRMS Settings if phone is lost.

pages.title: Are push notifications supported?
pages.description: Notification preferences are in employee profile — delivery depends on org mobile push configuration.

pages.title: Where is the chart type reference?
pages.description: Documentation → Charts explains donut, bar, area, line, funnel, and treemap usage.

pages.title: Do charts respect filters?
pages.description: Yes — summary strip charts on list screens recalculate when SHOW, team, date, or text filters change.

pages.title: What is a utilization donut?
pages.description: Billable vs available hours ratio for a person or team — common on HRMS dashboard and mobile insights.

pages.title: What is a segment bar?
pages.description: Horizontal stacked bar showing proportional mix (e.g. invoice status or task status) with color legend.

pages.title: Why is a chart empty?
pages.description: No data in the active filter scope — widen date range, clear text filter, or check team selection.

pages.title: Can I export chart data?
pages.description: Export list/register actions may include summary data — chart-specific export depends on screen implementation.

pages.title: What is team capacity chart?
pages.description: Project → Team Capacity — shows allocation vs availability for staffing planning.

pages.title: How do I read the monthly billing bar?
pages.description: HRMS Invoice summary — invoiced amount by month within selected fiscal year.

pages.title: Who is a workspace administrator?
pages.description: Users with App Config access, HRMS Settings, or elevated role templates — documented in Admin guide.

pages.title: How are permissions assigned?
pages.description: Role templates in Application Configuration attach to org units; users inherit via team membership.

pages.title: What is the difference between role and org config?
pages.description: Org nodes hold dropdown data and lists; role nodes hold CRUD and module visibility flags.

pages.title: Can I give someone read-only project access?
pages.description: Clone a manager role, disable create/update/delete flags on project permission groups, assign to org unit.

pages.title: Where is Application Configuration?
pages.description: HRMS → Application Configuration (/hrms/appconfig) — requires appconfigEnabled.

pages.title: What is HRMS Settings vs App Config?
pages.description: Settings = devices, schedulers, company info. App Config = org/role trees for lists and permissions.

pages.title: How do I audit permission changes?
pages.description: Rely on server audit logs and change-management — test role changes on a child org unit before Root edits.

pages.title: Why can a user see a button but get an error on click?
pages.description: UI visibility flags may differ from API enforcement — verify both module and CRUD permission groups.

pages.title: What is team scope?
pages.description: Filters data to the user's org unit/team — managers see their tree unless given broader scope.

pages.title: How do I request access for a new hire?
pages.description: HR creates employee record, assigns team and role — user receives activation email.

pages.title: Page loads but data is empty
pages.description: Check team filter, SHOW preset, and date range. Confirm you have list permission for that module.

pages.title: Changes not saving
pages.description: Look for validation errors, unsaved indicator, or network errors in browser dev tools. Confirm update permission on your role.

pages.title: Dropdown missing a new value
pages.description: App Config change may be on wrong org node — verify user's team inheritance and refresh the form.

pages.title: Timesheet row rejected
pages.description: Check daily hour cap, closed project, week lock, or missing work item permission.

pages.title: Invoice total looks wrong
pages.description: Compare billable pool on details vs timesheet approvals for the billing period.

pages.title: SSO loop back to login
pages.description: Clear cookies, try incognito, contact admin to verify IdP app registration and user provisioning.

pages.title: Mobile QR won't scan
pages.description: Renew web session, check camera permission, confirm device registration enabled in settings.

pages.title: Search returns no results
pages.description: Try shorter keywords, verify module access, and ensure spelling matches indexed fields.

pages.title: Chart shows stale numbers
pages.description: Hard refresh browser; charts refresh on filter change — cached session rarely stale.

pages.title: Still stuck — who do I contact?
pages.description: Your Tracopus workspace administrator or internal IT support with screen URL, username, and timestamp.

pages.title: Who can open Application Configuration?
pages.description: Users whose role has hrmsModules.appconfigEnabled set to true (see Access control → HRMS Modules Access). Without this flag the /hrms/appconfig route is hidden from the sidebar.

pages.title: What is the difference between Settings and App Config?
pages.description: Settings (/hrms/settings) covers operational cards: devices, schedulers, company info, locale. App Config is the hierarchical org/role tree that drives dropdown lists, feature togg

pages.title: Why do I see an empty screen or “no config” message?
pages.description: Ensure your user team has a valid org node selected. The page loads config via initializeConfig(currentUserTeamId) on mount. If the team is not mapped to an org unit, contact a sup

pages.title: Can I use App Config on mobile?
pages.description: No — Application Configuration is a desktop admin screen only. Use a full browser session; mobile HRMS apps do not expose this route.

pages.title: How do I get Site Admin–level access?
pages.description: An existing admin must enable appconfigEnabled on your role template, assign that role to your org unit via Role Bar, and ensure your user belongs to the correct team.

pages.title: What is the difference between org nodes and role nodes?
pages.description: Org nodes (type=org) store application data: departments, categoryMap, notification emails. Role nodes (type=role) store permission templates: CRUD flags, timesheet windows, module

pages.title: What does the chain icon do?
pages.description: Linked chain (fa-chain) = inherit parentValue from the parent org unit. Broken chain (fa-chain-broken, overridden=true) = this node stores its own value. Click the chain button on

pages.title: What happens when I lock a setting?
pages.description: locked=true prevents child org units from overriding that key. Combined with hidden=true, non-admin users may not see the block at all. Use lock on Root for enterprise-wide standar

pages.title: Should I edit Root or a child team?
pages.description: Edit Root for defaults that apply everywhere. Edit a child org unit only when that team needs a local override (regional departments, team-specific notification list). Always test

pages.title: How do I create a new org unit or team node?
pages.description: Organization tab → select parent → (+) add child. Set name, parent, and category in the hero bar → save identity fields. New nodes inherit all parent config until you break the cha

pages.title: What does parentLocked mean?
pages.description: When the parent node has locked a key, child nodes show parentLocked and cannot change inherit/lock/hide on that item — the chain and lock buttons are disabled.

pages.title: When do I need to click Save?
pages.description: Module-level Save persists value changes (updateConfig). Property-only edits (name, parent, category, overridden, locked, hidden) use updateConfigProperty and may save per-field. W

pages.title: What do the All / Overridden / Locked filters do?
pages.description: All — every visible config on the selected node. Overridden — keys where this node broke inheritance. Locked — keys locked on this node (children cannot override). Use with the sea

pages.title: Do UI edits overwrite org.json on disk?
pages.description: No. org.json and role.json seed deployment. Runtime edits persist to the database. Re-deploying from JSON without migration can overwrite DB changes — export or document before maj

pages.title: Can I undo a change?
pages.description: There is no global undo. Re-link the chain to inherit parent again, or manually restore previous values. For roles, clone Site Admin to a backup role before large permission edits.

pages.title: Why is Save disabled or missing?
pages.description: You may lack appconfigEnabled, the module may be disabled on this node, or the key may be parentLocked. Check role permissions and parent lock state.

pages.title: Where do employee dropdown values come from?
pages.description: HRMS module keys: band, grade, department, designation, skills, etc. Changes appear on the employee create wizard and profile after users refresh or open a new form.

pages.title: What is categoryMap used for?
pages.description: Three-level tree: Service Line → Delivery Category → Task Category. Drives billable categorization on timesheets, project/deliverable forms, and reporting. Large trees affect picke

pages.title: What is practiceMap?
pages.description: Two-level HR practice hierarchy (Primary → Secondary Practice) on employee profiles. Used for staffing filters and practice-based analytics, separate from project categoryMap.

pages.title: How do notification email lists work?
pages.description: Keys like defaultNotificationEmails, defaultPurchaseOrderNotificationEmails set default distribution when projects or POs trigger workflow emails. Finance-specific keys route to fi

pages.title: What are NONPROJECT categories?
pages.description: NONPROJECT module → taskActCategory lists non-billable timesheet types (meetings, training, leave). excludeAdditionalFieldsForCategory hides extra fields for quick entry on Leave/H

pages.title: Can I enable multi service line estimates?
pages.description: PROJECT toggles: enableServiceLineEstimate, enableServiceLineSelection, enableCategorySelection. When enabled, projects and POs show estimate panels per service line — coordinate w

pages.title: Can I delete a categoryMap leaf used in old timesheets?
pages.description: Avoid hard deletes. Historical rows reference leaf IDs/names. Prefer stopping new use (hide/lock at Root) while retaining legacy values for reports.

pages.title: How do I bulk-add list values?
pages.description: In any list config block, use the multi-add textarea (toggle from single-line add) and paste one value per line from Excel, then save the module.

pages.title: How are roles assigned to users?
pages.description: Roles attach to org units via ApplicationConfigRoleBar on an org node — not directly on user records. Users inherit the role mapped to their team’s org unit.

pages.title: How do I create a custom Manager role?
pages.description: Roles tab → (+) new role → configure module visibility and permission groups → save. Start from Site Admin and disable delete/archive/appconfig flags. Assign via Role Bar on delive

pages.title: Why can a user see a menu item but not perform actions?
pages.description: Module visibility (*Enabled in hrmsModules/projectModules) is separate from CRUD groups (createEnabled, editEnabled). Enable both the module flag and the action flag in the correct

pages.title: What is defaultRedirectPage?
pages.description: Landing slug when the user opens a module (e.g. dashboard, activites, bidrequests). Set per role under HRMS/Project/Sales Modules Access.

pages.title: How do report permissions work?
pages.description: reporting group lists each report type as a boolean. Users only see reports they are allowed to run in the REPORT dropdown.

pages.title: Can managers edit other employees’ timesheets?
pages.description: Controlled by timeSheet.switchEmployeesEnabled, enableTimeSheetEdit, and related work-item flags. Set on the manager’s role template, not per user.

pages.title: Why can’t a user log time for last week?
pages.description: Check enableTimeSheetEdit, enablePastTimeSheetView, disableLastMonthAfterXDays, and work-item window flags (disableProjectWorkItemCreateBeforeXWorkingDays, etc.) on their role.
keywords: app config · timesheet & work item rules

pages.title: What does disableLastMonthAfterXDays do?
pages.description: Locks the previous month’s timesheet after X days into the current month (e.g. 5 = after the 5th, prior month is read-only). Common payroll control.
keywords: app config · timesheet & work item rules

pages.title: What is maxHoursAllowedToEnter?
pages.description: Daily or per-entry hour cap validation on timesheet rows. Prevents accidental 24+ hour entries.
keywords: app config · timesheet & work item rules

pages.title: Why are non-project entries blocked?
pages.description: Review disableNonProjectWorkItemCreateBeforeXWorkingDays / AfterXWorkingDays and NONPROJECT categories in org config. Value -1 often means rule disabled — check your deployment’s c
keywords: app config · timesheet & work item rules

pages.title: Can users book leave for future dates?
pages.description: allowLeaveAndHolidayForFuture and allowLeaveAndHolidayForPast on the role control leave booking direction on non-project categories.
keywords: app config · timesheet & work item rules

pages.title: Dropdown missing a value I added in App Config
pages.description: Confirm you saved the module, selected the correct org node (user’s team scope), and refreshed the target form. Child teams inherit Root unless overridden — add the value on the no

pages.title: Permission change not taking effect
pages.description: Ask the user to log out and back in. Clear browser cache if menu items persist. Verify Role Bar mapping on the user’s org unit matches the role you edited.

pages.title: User sees App Config but changes fail
pages.description: UI may show read-only if parent locked keys or module is disabled. Check API errors in network tab — server enforces permissions independently.

pages.title: categoryMap picker is slow
pages.description: Tree too large or too many leaf nodes. Archive obsolete branches, use lock at Root to prevent duplicate local trees, and limit depth to three meaningful levels.

pages.title: Two teams see different department lists
pages.description: Expected if one team overrode HRMS → department on a child org node. Compare org nodes in App Config with Overridden filter.

pages.title: When do users see config changes?
pages.description: List values: usually next page load. Permissions: often next session. Some caches may delay up to a few minutes — document your org’s refresh policy.
